icc_identification.method: moment regression of squared session deviations on 1/m_s
icc_identification.note: The bootstrap interval spans an order of magnitude and its fail-closed upper bound (0.5317) is worse than the assumed 0.20. The ICC route is therefore rejected as a power lever. The transferable parameter is the realized contrast SD, which needs no ICC because it is measured at session level directly.

scenarios.sd_basis: Popoviciu bound b=30 / sqrt(m_eff), ICC=0.20 ASSUMED

scenarios.encoding: signed excursion magnitude, GC estimand family
scenarios.sd_basis: GC realized paired-session contrast SD, MEASURED n=234

source_run.multiplicity: single preregistered configuration, alpha=0.05, no Bonferroni

transfer_justification: GC and NQ Gate 1 share the same event family (BigTrap2Absorption), the same runner lineage (edgelab.research.bt2_gate1_all5), the same paired within-CME-session contrast K_ABS - N_RAND, the same equal-session weighting, the same 234-session sample size, and the same replication design (replications=10000, seed=20260821). GC outcomes are already open, so reading them opens nothing new. Two independent margins make the transfer conservative rather than optimistic for NQ: (1) NQ cells cap excursions at 5-30 ticks over 25-250 horizons, far tighter than GC's tick_cap=2000 / clock_cap_seconds=900, and a tighter cap can only reduce event-level outcome variance; (2) NQ has 652.5 events per session against GC's 72.4, which can only reduce the sampling component of session-level variance. The transferred SD is therefore an upper bound for NQ under the same estimand, not a point estimate.
